decision: Do not automatically prioritize player-support and cursor-target chunks in the g23 production profile.
conclusions: The authority lease contract activated and reprioritized existing demand without expanding terrain residency.
The proposed automatic production policy did not improve the first post-relocation edit in either run order.
Committed edits already use the highest scheduler priority; the remaining delay is after acceptance and authority commit, chiefly in readiness and publication work.
The g23 production default remains disabled. Tilde+R and the command-line override retain an explicit diagnostic path only.
This rejection does not promote a GPU backend and does not weaken CPU correctness authority.
claim_boundary: Two order-balanced paired diagnostics reject this policy for the pinned system. They do not prove that all narrower foreground scheduling policies are universally harmful.
